messages:
arjun: Heads-up — product wants to add two high-cardinality audit events: file.uploaded and file.downloaded coming from S3 integrations. Request: full payload for compliance. Concern: one customer can generate 50k events/min. How do we handle schema, validation, KMS, and cost?

rachel: We must avoid logging sensitive headers and pre-signed URLs. KMS envelope encryption for any payload fields marked secret. Also need schema versioning so we can roll forward/back. :lock: :eyes:

mikhail: High-level ops concerns: indexing every payload field into ES will bankrupt us. Options: 1) index a small summary + pointer to raw blob in compressed S3, 2) keep full raw events in cold storage behind access controls, 3) sample events for search. Also recommend partitioning by tenant id in Kafka and batching writes.

paula: From the last load test, ingest queue went to 120k/s and tail latency spiked ~5s; our backpressure started dropping at the API layer. We need per-tenant rate limits, quotas, and a graceful 429 with Retry-After. Also consider a short-term throttle tier for event-heavy customers.

jen: Legal and product: many customers require a complete trace for audits. They'll accept cold storage + signed manifest if we provide an on-demand restore within SLA. Can we offer a "full-audit" add-on that stores raw events for 90 days unindexed but retrievable?

nina: Customer ops: they want signed events and schema validation so their SIEM ingestion is deterministic. If we change schema, we must version and give migration guidance.

arjun: Proposed schema contract (v1) — strict event wrapper, small indexed metadata, rest opaque pointer. Example payload: 
```json
{
  "audit_version": "redwood_audit_v1",
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "event_type": "file.uploaded",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-12T14:23:00Z",
  "indexed": { "file_size": 12345, "result": "success" },
  "raw_blob_s3": "s3://redwood-audit/t-123/2025/11/12/abcd.snappy",
  "signature": "base64sig.."
}
```
We should enforce JSON Schema on the API and return 422 for invalid payloads.

mikhail: Ingestion infra changes: batch at API -> produce compressed protobuf/snappy to Kafka. Use tenant-based partitioning and a small producer-side buffer to group messages (100 ms window or 1k msgs). Consumers will write compressed objects to S3 and write a lightweight index doc to ES (tenant, event_type, ts, pointer). This reduces ES doc count and costs ~10x.

paula: For backpressure: add a fast path that rejects large raw uploads and a fallback: accept metadata but return a 202 with a signed upload URL to a customer-specific bucket with server-side encryption. Also add short-circuit sampling: if tenant exceeds X tps, only 1/N events get full retention; rest are summarized.

rachel: KMS note: per-tenant DEK generation is good for isolation but causes an extra KMS call per rotation. Suggest we use envelope encryption with cached DEKs in the service (TTL'd) and rotate monthly. For retrieval, rotate without re-encrypting by keeping previous DEK versions for a grace period. Document this in runbook.

arjun: Cost math (rough): ES index cost ~ $0.0006/doc/month if fully indexed. 50k/min ~ 72M docs/day -> impossible. Strategy: index small skeleton ~1-2 fields per event, compressed raw in S3 (cheap), and offer paid retrieval. Also expose per-tenant unit metrics so sales can talk about pricing for high-volume retention.

ops-bot: Incident note: tested tenant t-999 throttle in staging. Backpressure triggered at 10k/s, 429 ramped as expected.

audit-bot: New policy added: audit_event_schema_v1.json in repo "infra/audit/schemas". PR: #4521.

jen: Action items: 1) write strict JSON schema + examples (owners: arjun/rachel), 2) infra design doc for batch ingestion & S3-pointer pattern (owner: mikhail), 3) runbook for KMS DEK caching + rotation (owner: rachel), 4) pricing proposal for high-volume retention (owner: jen).

paula: I'll schedule a load test for next Tue with 150k/s for 30m, include lifecycle: full retention vs sampled.

arjun: Sounds good. Quick win: enforce schema + pointer-only indexing today, follow-ups for KMS and pricing. :thumbsup:

mikhail: +1. I'll draft the infra doc and include producer batching knobs and backpressure signals (Retry-After + X-Queue-Depth).

rachel: I'll start the schema and runbook. We should also add an FAQ for customers about what we redact and how to request full data.

nina: I'll prep a customer-facing note and coordinate with sales for the add-on.

paula: :white_check_mark:

arjun: Thanks all — let's sync after docs are up.
